steps.text: 'Pfft! Bleh! Ugh!'
'Who dug this hole in the road? I almost broke my back, and my mouth's full of sand!'
The red-headed Kuranta climbs out of the sand hole, looking quite the worse for wear. She is wearing a burdenbeast skull on her foot, having stepped right through the top of it.
She turns around to yell at the empty desert, hardly bothering to even pat the dust and sand off herself.
She does not even know whom she is yelling at, but the more she thinks about it, the angrier she gets. She pulls the skull off her foot and throws it far away.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Which caravan didn't even bother to look for a burdenbeast that fell into a hole? Those bones almost went through my thigh!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: And why were they carrying a whole bunch of linen instead of something worth money? *Sargon expletive* All that trouble, and I come back nearly empty-handed!
Narantuya lifts the object she has been holding. It was the only thing that shined gold in the hole, so she took it with her on her way out.
She peruses her lone souvenir in the bright sunlight.
The elaborate patterns on the golden lamp glow brightly.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's made of gold? Should be worth a pretty good sum! Guess it was a blessing in disguise!
Narantuya wipes the lamp on her clothes, and it casts its golden reflection upon her face.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wait, are those words engraved on it?
'To Asaf of Fountain Town. Happy eighth birthday. Love, Mother.'
'Treasure it, for it will illuminate all the treasures I left for you.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Damned rich people. They give their kids presents made of solid gold?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Well, I guess it'll be justice for all the poor folks they've been stepping on when I turn this golden lamp into meat and wine for my stomach at the bazaar!
Narantuya takes a few steps, then stops. She looks down again at the engraved words.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'Treasures'. I read that right, didn't I? It says 'treasures'?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Treasures left behind by such wealthy people...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: They must be worth even more than this golden lamp!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Hey, old man! Show your face! I've got questions for you!

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: What's the rush? Have a couple of drinks to cool down.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You've been to more places in this desert than I have. Have you heard of a 'Fountain Town'?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Of course! Fountain Town is... hehe.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Spit it out!

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: What is this? Vengeance, or robbery?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...It's a wealthy place, isn't it? Tell me where it is.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: No rush, no rush, have a couple of drinks with me and I'll tell you.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Fine, I was thirsty anyway.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Why are you only pouring one? Aren't you drinking?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Sure am. This one's mine.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What about mine?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Gotta pay up first.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Like I ever owed you booze money. How much?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: One hundred... no, two hundred dinars.
Narantuya's hand, which was reaching for the coin bag on her belt, freezes in mid-air. With clenched teeth, she asks—

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You think your diluted arak is worth two hundred dinars a cup?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: But the information you're looking for is.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: It's none of my business what business you have at Fountain Town, whether you were hired to bump somebody off, or found a treasure map for a pot of gold...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Two hundred dinars, then? Fine, I'll pay. Bring the booze!

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Guessed right, didn't I? Hey, no need to glare. You think this bundle of old bones is gonna steal your treasure?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Bah, paying two hundred dinars doesn't make your swill taste any better!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: One cup's not enough to loosen your lips? Fine, I'll have another!
Narantuya throws her whole coin bag at the man. It is unclear whether she is grimacing because the alcohol is burning her throat, or the frustration is burning her heart.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What are you sitting there for? Pour! There's gotta be at least two hundred dinars in the bag!

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Two hundred was for the first cup. The second's gonna cost you four hundred.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Now, now, don't get violent with me, Narantuya. I know you're good, but every bazaar has its rules, and my rule is...

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: No refunds.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: If one cup's enough for you, that's fine too. So many sand bandits are looking to make their fortune in this desert, someone's gotta be willing to buy a couple of cups.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'll be back in half an hour with the money... And you better not tell anyone.
Narantuya touches the scimitar on her belt and puts on her fiercest expression.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Sure, sure...
Thump.
The sound of the heavy coin bag hitting the counter wakes the fake liquor seller with such a fright that he falls to the ground.
Narantuya grabs the bottle from behind the counter and takes a swig from it.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What are you doing? Count them.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Y-You've gotta have at least a thousand dinars in this bag! Don't tell me...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No need to get excited. I just sold a burdenbeast to a caravan.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Since when did you have a burdenbeast?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Since just now. Stole it from a passing caravan.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Don't tell me it was the same caravan.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It was the same caravan.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Did those idiots not realize?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Nope. Wanna know how it went down?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Then tell me where this *Sargon expletive* Fountain Town is!

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Alright, alright, no rush, lemme pour you a cup—from my special collection. Not diluted at all.
Narantuya downs the spirit and looks at the 'map' the fake liquor seller gave her.
Little more than a napkin with a few lines drawn on it, representing hills and roads.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's at least a three or four day journey... are you sure?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: When have I ever scammed anyone... I mean, when have I ever scammed you?

spans.text: When have I ever scammed anyone... I mean, when have I ever scammed

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: But you're right, it's a long way. Way too long to walk.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Are you trying to sell me your old and deaf burdenbeast? The one you have tied up behind the tent?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: You catch on quick! I'll give you a good price, eight hundred dinars!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's hauled goods for you your entire life without getting a single decent meal, and now you want to sell it to me?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Well, if you won't buy it, I guess I'm having meat for dinner.
Narantuya shakes her head.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...What I mean is, you're selling it short. I think it's worth a thousand dinars, at least.
Narantuya takes the 'map', downs the rest of the cup's contents, and turns around to leave.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Hey, Narantuya! You didn't tell me how the caravan didn't notice that you stole their burdenbeast!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I just dangled some wheat in front of its face, and it came with me quietly.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: That's all? How boring.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Serves them right for all the dirty business they do, though!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Serves 'em right... Yeah. Absolutely.
The moment Narantuya leaves, the fake liquor seller starts quickly packing up his tent.

steps.name: Drunken Passerby
steps.text: Closing shop so early?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Yeah, come back tomorrow... No, I won't be here tomorrow. Hope we meet again!

steps.name: Drunken Passerby
steps.text: What, you owe someone money?

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: Just scammed a madwoman. Gotta get out of town before she comes back... Now stop asking questions and scram!
The fake liquor seller runs out the tent with his luggage on his back, only to realize that there is only a rope tied to the stake where he leashed his burdenbeast.

steps.name: Fake Liquor Seller
steps.text: *Sargon expletive*! Narantuya! So it was MY burdenbeast that you stole!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Damn, spent all my money before I even caught a glimpse of the treasure.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Don't disappoint me, sweet treasure... *hic*... it better be all gold coins inside a chest made of solid gold!
Narantuya climbs to the top of the hill and compares the map with the view in front of her.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Shouldn't there be a hill here?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Was I holding it upside down?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Oh! Now I see a village. That's more like it.
Narantuya rubs her eyes and casts her gaze forward, but her vision remains blurred.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: That drink made me even more thirsty. Gotta find a place with a well to spend the night. Hopefully a burdenbeast to carry me too...
Narantuya stands up with unsteady legs.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Damn, how could this stuff be so strong?
Narantuya takes a few wobbly steps forward and steps into a musbeast hole, causing her to fall and roll down the slopes.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Ow! My head!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'm never drinking fake liquor again!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...My head hurts!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Where am I... why does it feel so wet... is it raining?
Narantuya opens her eyes and sees a familiar burdenbeast licking her face excitedly.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What's going on?!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: I found the burdenbeast! Hey, aren't you that girl who sold it to me?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What happened to me...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Oh no, the map!
Narantuya frantically searches herself and is relieved to find that the creased map is still there.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Phew... you didn't touch my stuff, did you?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We just arrived, following the burdenbeast's tracks. Did you fall from the hill? Look at all the bruises on you...

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: You're not thinking of buying it back, are you? It'll cost you at least three thousand dinars.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No, I'm not...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wait, that's double the price, isn't it?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We're counting on this old burdenbeast to find water for us! Well, it found you first.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Maybe it just smelled a familiar liquor... Are you guys heading this way too?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Are you passing by Fountain Town? The place marked on this map...

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: ...You call this a 'map'?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I bought it with the money I sold the burdenbeast for. Maybe I'm holding it upside down. This is the place where Fountain Town should be...

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Hah, you got scammed, lady. This is just a bunch of scribbles!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I got scammed?!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Now I remember. Fountain Town was a really wealthy place.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: But it fell on hard times a few decades ago, and everyone moved away. There's only a Fountain Village now, which happens to be in the same direction we're headed.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (But the golden lamp said 'Fountain Town'. Are people just used to the old name?)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: If it's the same direction, can you take me along on the way? I'll pay you once we get there.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We don't do credit. Small business.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Then... how about I guard your caravan? You won't need to pay me.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: You see those thirty big, burly, armed men over there? They're our guards.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I can feed your burdenbeasts?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We have dedicated keepers that work around the clock in shifts.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What DO you need then?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Hm... we could use someone to collect the burdenbeast dung behind us. It's useful as fuel. But you'll have to walk behind the caravan all day. Not the sort of work most people are willing to do.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I'll do it!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (I'll just pick a strong and healthy burdenbeast and run away with it when we're near the place!)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (He wanted to sell it back for twice the price! That's highway robbery! Someone should teach you a lesson!)

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Hey, thanks. Must be hard work, eating sand and dust all day in the rear.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: There's more than just sand... What the hell are you feeding these burdenbeasts?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You got any water? I want to wash my face and hands.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: You know how precious water is in the desert. Bear with it.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: I'm just here to collect what you picked up today... Wait, you filled this whole cart with the stuff?!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I just want to know when we get to Fountain Village.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We're almost there.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Are we there yet?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Almost—

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Are the there yet?!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Almost, really!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: We're not there yet... Oh, screw this. Call over your thirty guards.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: What for?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Because next time you say 'almost', I'm putting my fist in your face. But I need your guards there so you can't say I'm bullying you.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We'll be there soon! Trust me!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Look, right over there! You see those dozen houses on the bank of the river? We've been going around it, but this time we're really almost there!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Going around it? What d'you mean?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: We're running a business here! All the caravans go around that poor, backwater place.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (Poor, backwater place? If you knew there was treasure there...)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So you never intended to take me to Fountain Village?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Our deal was just to take you along on the way.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'Take me along'? You had me shoveling dung behind the caravan!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'd beat you to a pulp if I wasn't so tired... Fine, I'll go there myself! You can pick up this stuff yourself!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Don't throw it at me!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Now my silk tunic's all dirty! I'm deducting this from your pay!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You're not paying me anything!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Don't care. Any damage is to be paid back at three times the original price. Right now, you owe me 2700 dinars, plus a ten percent handling fee if you pay in gold certificates.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I don't have any money on me.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: I can loan you some. The interest-rate per day is...

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: What's that sound... why are you grinding your teeth like that?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Now, now, no need to get violent. You have something pretty valuable on your belt, don't you?
Narantuya looks down at her belt. The golden lamp, which she had wrapped in a tattered piece of cloth. The handle has become exposed, and its golden glow shines brightly.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Not this.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: ...I have thirty guards.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: And I have four blades. You're welcome to try.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Come on! You're being as unreasonable as a sand bandit! We've done business before, haven't we?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Unreasonable? I... I AM a sand bandit!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Well, even sand bandits have to buy food and sell their stolen wares. I can at least give you a price for your trinket. You might even end up selling it to me anyway.
Narantuya angrily takes out the lamp and presses it against the caravan leader's nose.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You think I care about your money? You see this? Made of solid gold! It's enough to buy all your burdenbeasts with change to spare!

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Solid gold? Doesn't look that way to me.
The caravan leader scratches the side of the golden lamp lightly with his fingernail, revealing the dull color underneath.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: See? It's copper on the inside with a layer of golden paint... Hah, got scammed by someone else, didn't you?

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Though it's good craftsmanship, I'll give it that. Might have fooled me, if I were a little less knowledgeable.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: But if I knew you were this gullible, I'd have struck a harder bargain when I bought your burdenbeast... haha....
Every word from the caravan leader makes Narantuya's expression grow darker. She clutches the 'golden' lamp so hard it is almost as if she is trying to crush it.
She looks up at the caravan leader, whose mouth continues to move, babbling words that she is not listening to. All she knows that they irritate her.
She raises her fist.

steps.name: Caravan Leader
steps.text: Y-You hit me! Guards! Where are my thirty guards? Help!
Narantuya is tired, thirsty, hungry, and angry.
She reaches towards her belt and finds her empty coin bag. She is also poor.
Then, she finds the lamp, and she angrily tosses it towards the sky.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: *Sargon expletive*!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This is all your fault!
The lamp spins in the air a few times, then falls straight back down, almost hitting her in the face.
It falls on the sand, the engraved side facing up. Narantuya remembers the words without having to look.

a.text: '...it will illuminate all the treasures I left for you.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Some damned treasure.
Narantuya drags her exhausted hide forward. She is not sure where she is going, as long as it is away from the lamp.
But then, she recalls the other line etched on it—

a.text: 'To Asaf of Fountain Town. Happy eighth birthday. Love, Mother.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: *Sigh*...
Narantuya angrily kicks the sand and hits a hard rock. It hurts so much it brings tears to her eyes.
She slows down and eventually turns around to pick up the lamp.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Never give up, even if it's just a tiny sliver of hope... For the treasure...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Don't let me down this time.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This is Fountain Town... I mean, Fountain Village, right?

steps.name: Wary Villager
steps.text: Who are you looking for?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Does someone by the name of Asaf live here?

steps.name: Wary Villager
steps.text: What do you want with him? I've never seen you around these parts!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's a long story. Bring him over—I have something to give him.

steps.name: Worried Villager
steps.text: Is someone looking for old Asaf? He's really sick. The mayor said no one is to go near his house.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Old Asaf?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: There must be a mistake. The Asaf I'm looking for is eight years old.

steps.name: Wary Villager
steps.text: There's only ever been one Asaf in Fountain Village, and he's a hundred and one.

steps.name: Worried Villager
steps.text: He might've even broken our age record, if his children hadn't moved away and refused to take care of him...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: There's no one taking care of him?

steps.name: Wary Villager
steps.text: What's it to you? I'm still not letting you in our village!
With a sigh, Narantuya takes out the golden lamp, carefully placing her thumb to hide where the paint was scratched off.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Let me see him. You can have this, if he's really the one I'm looking for.
The villagers look at the golden object, then at each other hesitantly.
Narantuya walks into the tiny hut. The air is filled with dust and the strong smell of herbs.
A withered old man lies on the bed, his chest heaving up and down, and a strange rattle coming from his throat.
Narantuya can see his life fading before her eyes.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wait! Don't... not yet!
Narantuya dashes towards the bed and puts the slightly misshapen lamp in the old man's hand.
Holding his withered hand, she lifts the lamp into the sunlight, and it reflects its golden glow in the old man's eyes.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Look, there are words etched here! Let me read them for you—
'To Asaf of Fountain Town. Happy eighth birthday. Love, Mother.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You're Asaf, right? This was a birthday present from your mom, but an accident happened and it never reached you.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Do you hear me, Asaf? I'm giving you the golden lamp that your mom gave you as a present!
The old man's eyes go wide and his lips quiver, but no coherent words come out of them.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yes, your mom. You remember her, right?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Do you remember where this 'treasure' she talked about is?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Trea—sure. Treasure!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I didn't catch that. Say it again?
Narantuya leans down, putting her ears towards the old man's mouth, only to feel that his hands seem to have regained a little bit of strength.
He clutches the golden lamp and presses it against his chest, above his heart.
Then, he slowly reaches out towards the single ray of sunlight shining through the roof.
'To Asaf of Fountain Town...'
'...it will illuminate all the treasures I left for you.'
The sun shines upon the old man's palm and face. Narantuya does not know what he saw in the sunlight, but she sees a content smile on his face.
The old man closes his eyes and mutters softly...

steps.name: Dying Old Man
steps.text: ...I see it, Mother.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So where's the treasure?
The old man opens his eyes irritably, and Narantuya could swear that he rolled his eyes at her.
He opens his lips again, and Narantuya leans forward—

steps.name: Wary Villager
steps.text: She's the one who insisted on seeing Asaf, mayor!

steps.name: Worried Villager
steps.text: She had gold on her! Said she would give it to us!
Narantuya does not answer. She draws her knife and plunges it in the ground.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Have you prepared a grave for him?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Fine.
Narantuya picks a withered tree and buries the old man under it, along with the lamp.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Sorry it's so far away. They won't let me bury you in the village. Wasn't easy, carrying you all the way here.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This hilltop overlooks Fountain Village, so you'll always be able to see it if you miss home.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: And the tree'll give you shade, so that the sand won't burn your back.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...It'll also tell me where you are, if I ever come through here again.
Narantuya leans against the tree and wiggles her hands, which had become numb from the exertion.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: All that effort and not a single coin to show for it. Never thought I'd have to bury someone I've never met before.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So the treasure I was looking for was just a mother's blessings for her child...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'd already thrown the lamp away and was totally ready to leave, but then I thought about that little boy sitting by the door, waiting for his birthday present...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Who knew he'd been waiting that long?
Narantuya pats the withered tree, and a hollow sound comes out of it.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Well, that was a total loss. I'm never doing this again.
Narantuya sighs and stands up. In one last act of frustration, she punches the withered tree.
Crack—
It seems she punched it a little too hard. A long crack appears in the trunk, revealing the hollow within.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Please don't be dried burdenbeast dung.
Narantuya stretches her hand into the hollow, and finds a heavy and strangely-shaped object.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...You've got to be kidding me.
It is a goblet etched with elaborate patterns, with gems embedded across its surface. The form and craftsmanship are on a completely different level from the lamp she just buried.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Oh please—
Narantuya lifts it before her eyes, and it shines bright gold under the setting sun.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What the hell is going on?!
Narantuya examines the golden goblet carefully.
In the last light of dusk, she seems to see some delicate etchings on the bottom, looking strangely like...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No!
Narantuya closes her eyes and lies down on the sand, still clutching the goblet.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Not now... I'm too tired for this right now...
